title: How Can My Prayers Help Others? | Sri Daya Mata
formattedMarkdown:
# How Can My Prayers Help Others?

### A Spiritual Discourse by Sri Daya Mata
*Third President of Self-Realization Fellowship / Yogoda Satsanga Society of India*

---

### Introduction: The Sacred Bond of Prayer

Many times, earnest seekers ask, "How can my humble prayers truly help another soul? Can my quiet thoughts reach across miles to heal a loved one or bring peace to a world in turmoil?" Sri Daya Mata, one of the most beloved direct disciples of Paramahansa Yogananda, answered these questions with the profound assurance of one who lived in constant communion with the Divine. 

She taught that prayer is not merely a sentimental gesture or a form of wishful thinking. It is a precise, scientific laws-of-spirituality in action. When we pray for others, we are not trying to change God's mind; rather, we are aligning ourselves with His divine laws so that His infinite grace, healing, and love can flow through us to those in need. We become instruments of the Divine Mother, channeling Her boundless compassion into a world that is thirsting for comfort.

> "When you pray for others, you are using the most powerful force in the universe—the power of Divine Love. But to make that prayer effective, you must first establish your own connection with the Divine Source. You must tune your instrument."

---

### The Science of Intercessory Prayer

Sri Daya Mata frequently drew upon the teachings of her Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda, to explain the mechanics of prayer. Paramahansaji taught that the human mind is like a powerful broadcasting and receiving station. When we think deeply, we emit subtle vibrational waves. When we pray with intense concentration, devotion, and a dynamic will, we project those waves out into the great ocean of Cosmic Consciousness.

Just as radio waves can travel instantly across the globe to be picked up by a receiver that is tuned to the correct frequency, so do our spiritual vibrations reach the souls of those for whom we pray. However, the efficacy of our prayers depends on two vital factors: the strength of our transmission and the receptivity of the receiver. 

To strengthen our transmission, we must clear our minds of restlessness, doubt, and selfishness. Through daily, deep meditation—using the scientific techniques of Kriya Yoga taught by Self-Realization Fellowship—we quiet the storms of the ego. In that stillness, our mind becomes a highly potent transmitter of God's light. 

---

### Tuning the Instrument of the Soul

How do we ensure that our prayers are not just empty words, but living conduits of Spirit? Sri Daya Mata emphasized that the quality of our devotion is paramount. When we pray, we must not approach God as beggars, but as His beloved children, claiming our divine birthright. 

We must first establish a loving relationship with Him. Whether we call upon Him as the Heavenly Father, the Divine Mother, Friend, or Beloved, we must feel His living presence in our hearts. When our hearts are filled with His love, our prayers for others become naturally effective, because it is no longer our small, limited ego praying, but the Divine Mother Herself praying through us.

> "Do not pray with a sense of doubt or anxiety. When you pray for another, surrender that soul completely into the loving hands of the Divine Mother. Say to Her: 'Lord, Thy will be done. Pour Thy healing light upon this soul, and let Thy love comfort them.'"

To pray effectively for others also requires that we cleanse our own hearts of resentment, anger, and judgment. If we harbor ill-will toward anyone, the channel of our prayer is obstructed. Unconditional love and forgiveness are the keys that unlock the floodgates of divine grace, allowing the pure waters of healing to flow unhindered to those in distress.

---

### The Power of Divine Will and Visualization

Sri Daya Mata taught that active, dynamic will is essential in prayer. We must not be passive onlookers. We must apply our concentration and visualization to help project the healing energy. 

During prayer, visualize the person you wish to help as being bathed in a brilliant, golden light—the divine light of Christ Consciousness. See that light penetrating every cell of their body, mind, and soul. Do not focus on their disease, their limitations, or their suffering, for what we focus on, we reinforce. Instead, visualize them as they truly are in Spirit: perfect, healthy, joyous, and free children of the Divine.

As you visualize this, direct your will to send the healing power. Rub your hands together briskly to sensitize them and draw in Cosmic Energy. Then, raise your hands and chant "Aum," projecting that life-giving force to the individual. This sacred technique, taught by Paramahansa Yogananda, physically and spiritually broadcasts the healing vibrations of the Holy Ghost to receptive souls everywhere.

---

### Practical Steps for Daily Intercessory Prayer

To build a powerful and consistent prayer life that serves as a beacon of hope for others, Sri Daya Mata recommended incorporating these practical habits into your spiritual routine:

* **Meditate First:** Never begin praying while your mind is still restless. Practice your concentration and meditation techniques first to interiorize your mind and connect with the peace of God.
* **Establish Devotion:** Offer your deep love to the Divine. Feel that you are resting in the lap of the Divine Mother, completely safe and loved.
* **Visualize Perfection:** See the person for whom you are praying surrounded and filled with the divine, golden light of the Infinite. See them as perfect and whole.
* **Employ Dynamic Will:** Direct your concentration to the spiritual eye (the seat of intuition and will between the eyebrows) and send a strong thought of healing, peace, and spiritual awakening.
* **Surrender the Outcome:** Release all anxiety and attachment to the results. Trust that God knows the deepest needs of that soul and will answer in the way that is best for their highest spiritual evolution.
* **Chant the Sacred Word:** Conclude your prayer by chanting "Aum" three times, sending the vibrations of Cosmic Energy into the universe for the healing of body, mind, and soul.

---

### The Healing Love of the Divine Mother

Ultimately, Sri Daya Mata reminded us that we are all brothers and sisters in the family of God. When we pray for others, we break down the walls of isolation and egoism that separate us. We realize our oneness in the Spirit. This act of selfless prayer not only brings healing and comfort to others, but it also purifies our own souls, drawing us closer to the divine goal of Self-realization.

Let us never underestimate the power of a single, sincere prayer offered with love. In the silent sanctuary of our hearts, we hold the key to blessing the entire world.

---

### A Closing Prayer and Blessing

> "O Divine Mother, Thou art the ultimate Healer. Thou art the source of all love, peace, and strength. We lay at Thy feet all those who are suffering in body, mind, or spirit. 
>
> Let Thy brilliant, healing light shine upon them. Dispel the darkness of fear, disease, and ignorance. Comfort their hearts and whisper to them of Thy eternal love. Make us pure channels of Thy grace, that we may bring Thy light to all whom we meet on this path of life."

*Jai Guru. Jai Ma.*
